payload.feature:
Decision 0042 (docs/decisions/0042-the-council-is-brokkrs-the-dialect-is-the-realms.md) is accepted; its first two slices have landed: the dialect library and the realm's `dialect`, and the SDD machine as a table with its loops, offices and this repository's migration to OpenSpec. This slice is 0042's last, ruling 8 exactly as written: `brokkr init` detects the dialect and `doctor` reports it. Read the decision first; it is the commission.

Ruling 8. `detect` in crates/brokkr-cli/src/init.rs learns the dialect beside the stack: a `.specify/` directory declares spec-kit; `openspec/config.yaml` declares OpenSpec; both present, init refuses to guess and asks (in the non-interactive path, it writes no dialect and says which two it found); neither, init writes no dialect and says an artifact phase will need one. The scaffolded `realms.json` carries `"dialect": "<name>"` when one was detected, and the scaffold's notes name the tool and the version the dialect file pins. `brokkr doctor` prints, for the realm map it reads, the realm's dialect, the tool binary it found on this machine and the version it measured against the dialect's pin, and each `requires` file present or missing — `ok`, `warn` or `fail` lines in doctor's existing voice — and a realm that names a dialect whose tool is absent is a `warn` that says the design route will refuse to run, not a `fail` of the whole doctor.

Tests. init's stack tests (crates/brokkr-cli/tests/init_stacks.rs and the init unit tests) gain the four detection cases — spec-kit, OpenSpec, both, neither — asserting the scaffolded map and the notes; doctor's tests (crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/tests.rs, init_doctor.rs) gain the dialect line for a realm with a dialect, one without, and one whose tool is missing; docs/guides/quickstart.md and repository-layout.md mention the line where they show doctor's output.

Constraints: the exact coverage gate (scripts/coverage-exact.sh, run with stdin closed: </dev/null) must stay at literal 100%; clippy -D warnings and fmt must stay clean; cargo test --workspace green; contracts/, fixtures/ and policy/phase-machine.json are read-only and this slice needs no contract change; the decision index docs/decisions/README.md must keep every row main carries in number order; do not name the private neighbours in prose; keep the CLI list "claude, codex or dsh" whenever a list of harnesses appears; commit in the repository's style and never push.


Two rules learned on an earlier fire, stated up front: every test that compares a path the product reports or prints against a path the test built compares them as `Path`s or after canonicalizing both sides — never as strings with a separator inside a component — because macOS's temp directory is a symlink and Windows paths carry a verbatim prefix and backslashes; and paths inside a hands box are POSIX strings joined with `/` whatever the host. The CI test job runs with `--no-fail-fast`, so a platform reports every failing binary at once.

A third rule, learned on the select fire: a guide or README that this slice touches is updated, never gutted — every reference section it carries today stays, revised for what changed, and the index lines that point at it stay true; deleting a section is a finding, not a simplification.

A fourth rule, learned on the dialect fire: the verify seat runs the workspace suite inside a bubblewrap box, so any test that drives a boxed step end to end nests a box and fails there while passing for you; every such test skips itself under the in-box marker `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX`, proves what it can at the compile layer or with an unboxed fake step, and says so in its comment. Prove the suite green inside a box yourself by setting the marker and running it.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

result.notes: Implemented dialect detection and scaffolded realm pins for spec-kit/OpenSpec, ambiguity and absence notes, and doctor reporting for dialect tools, pinned versions, and required files. Extended init/doctor unit and integration coverage plus both guides. cargo test --workspace passed normally and with BROKKR_HANDS_BOX=1; bundles/self compiled; fmt, clippy -D warnings, and literal exact coverage all passed; committed without pushing.

cargo test --workspace: 60 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed 9c8a95c against 544f1d8 (init.rs, doctor.rs, their tests, quickstart.md, repository-layout.md) with decision 0042 ruling 8 as the commission. Constraints re-checked and green: cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast exit 0; exact coverage re-derived from a fresh cargo +nightly llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --branch run and the gate's own LCOV accounting — 19363 DA records, 0 uncovered; 0 BRDA records with taken 0 or '-'; summary functions 1867/1867. (scripts/coverage-exact.sh itself will not run from a seat; I reproduced its evaluation.) No contract, fixture, policy/phase-machine.json or decision-index file touched; no harness list or private-neighbour name added; tracked tree clean, nothing pushed. The commission's literal test list is met: four detection cases in both the unit and the integration test, three doctor dialect cases, both guides carrying the new line. Two rules held: no test compares a product-reported path against a test-built path as a string, and no new test drives a boxed step, so none needs the BROKKR_HANDS_BOX skip (the sandbox refused an env-prefixed cargo invocation, so I could not re-run the suite under the marker myself; verify already did).

Eight findings remain; none is high or critical, so this is a residual and not a security-hold. Findings 1-3 are medium and return to the implementer.

1. MEDIUM (correctness) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/init.rs:1048, realms_json(). The scaffolded map hard-codes "path": ".", which resolves against the map file's own directory, i.e. the BUNDLE. But the dialect was detected from `repo`. For `brokkr init my-bundle` the two are different directories, so the realm points at the bundle. Reproduced: in a repo holding openspec/config.yaml, `brokkr init my-bundle` then `brokkr doctor` run from inside my-bundle exactly as init's own success line instructs prints `MISSING  dialect starter requires openspec/config.yaml: missing at .../my-bundle/./openspec/config.yaml` and exits 1 — init's output fails init's own preflight. Second consequence: `World::realm_for(repo)` compares canonical realm paths, so this map never matches the repository, and the realm's dialect and house never bind to a run against it. Third: the map lands inside the bundle directory, so it enters the compiled manifest's `files` digest map — verified, `"realms.json": "e05ef699…"` appears in `brokkr compile --bundle` output — which makes workspace data move the bundle digest, the thing crates/brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs:363-365 states must not happen.

2. MEDIUM (SECURITY) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs:364. doctor now spawns a binary named by realm-supplied data, unboxed, on the host: `probe(&dialect.tool.binary)` is `tool_version`, i.e. `Command::new(binary).arg("--version")`. crates/brokkr-runtime/src/dialect.rs:262-284 refuses absolute, drive-letter and `..` spellings for instruction paths but places no constraint at all on `tool.binary` beyond non-empty, so a path form is taken verbatim; `Command::new` resolves a value containing a separator against the current directory. Verified live: setting `"binary": "/bin/echo"` in a workspace's dialects/openspec.json made `brokkr doctor` execute it and print its output into the report. Reach: for every workspace scaffolded by `brokkr init .` — and for this repository, whose realms.json declares "openspec" and whose dialects/ is tracked — the dialect file is repository content, so whoever can land or hand over a branch chooses what doctor executes. That is arbitrary host execution as the operator on the one surface docs/guides/quickstart.md:126 advertises as executing nothing, and outside the box decision 0040 exists to keep repository-controlled content inside. Not high: it needs an operator-declared dialect plus write access to the operator's checkout, argv is fixed to `--version` and no shell is involved. Smallest fix consistent with the module's own discipline: judge `tool.binary` by spelling in `Dialect::check` the way instruction paths already are — a bare filename, no separator, no drive letter. Two riders on the same line: the probe has no timeout, so a hanging binary hangs doctor; and the probe's stdout is interpolated verbatim into the report line, so a hostile binary can forge the shape of an `ok` line.

3. MEDIUM (correctness) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/init.rs:1066, write_dialect(). init silently overwrites an operator's dialect files. Every other operator-owned thing init writes is refused by name before anything is written — bundle.json, both adapter declarations ("a tier is an operator's ruling, not a scaffold's"), each agent definition, each seat script, and, added by this slice, realms.json. `write_dialect` has no guard and no `create_new`. Reproduced: a hand-written bundle/dialects/openspec.json was replaced by the binary's embedded copy with no message and exit 0; the same holds for every dialects/<name>/*.md an operator may have tuned. The realms.json guard does not cover it — a directory can hold dialects/ without a map. This is the file that names the binary finding 2 executes.

4. LOW (correctness) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs:394-402. A missing `requires` file calls `report.missing`, which clears `healthy` and makes `brokkr doctor` exit 1, while a missing TOOL warns. Both block exactly the same thing — an artifact phase. Ruling 8 permits fail lines but frames the tool case as explicitly "not a `fail` of the whole doctor", and init can write a declaration doctor then rejects, because init's detection markers are not the dialect's requires set: `mkdir .specify && brokkr init .` writes "dialect": "speckit" and doctor then exits 1 on `.specify/templates/spec-template.md` and `.specify/scripts/bash/check-prerequisites.sh` (reproduced). Either warn on a missing required file, or detect on the same files the dialect requires.

5. LOW (docs) — the guides that show what init writes went stale on the file this slice added. docs/guides/quickstart.md:160-176 ("What it wrote") and every page under docs/guides/starters/ still list a scaffold with no realms.json and no dialects/ tree, and their transcribed digests no longer reproduce: the rust fixture now prints 0dc5a1a76e0f… where docs/guides/starters/rust.md:36 records d4b6f758d201…. That page states "if these commands ever stop being what `init` writes, a test goes red before this page goes stale" — no test enumerates the scaffold's file set or its digest, so nothing went red. quickstart.md:150-153 also still lists init's refusals without the new realms.json guard. The third rule of this fire says a guide this slice touches stays true, and quickstart.md is touched.

6. LOW (simplicity) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs:350 and 388-393 re-implement realm-root resolution that `World::path_of` already exposes; it is the same three lines as crates/brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs:395-402. The duplicate is also what puts the `/./` into every requires line doctor prints.

7. LOW (test integrity) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs:310-317 adds `#[cfg(test)] fn report_realm_house`, a test-only copy of the production dispatch kept so the five existing house tests need no edit. Those tests, including `assert_eq!(report.render(), "ok       house rules: no realms map; none declared")` at doctor/tests.rs:290, now assert against a function the binary never calls; the shipping `Ok(None)` arm emits two lines and no unit test covers it. Update the five tests and delete the shim.

8. INFO — `#[derive(Clone)]` on `DialectDetection` (init.rs:984) is never used (dead policy of exactly the kind doctor.rs:120-121 warns about). `version.contains(&dialect.tool.version)` (doctor.rs:365) is a substring test, so a dialect pinning "1.1" reports `ok` against a tool reporting 1.12.0. The two `Detected` arms of `detect_dialect` (init.rs:1027-1042) differ only in which constant they name.

I changed no files, made no commits and ticked no tasks. One residue to sweep: my reproduction scratch is at .forge/scratch/ (untracked, gitignored — `git status` is clean); the sandbox refused the rm, so it is still on disk.

Answered returned review findings 1-3. A subdirectory scaffold now records a relative realm path back to the repository detect inspected, and root realms.json/dialects workspace data are excluded from bundle identity. Dialect tool binaries must be bare PATH names, so realm data cannot select /bin/echo or another host path; measured output is terminal-sanitized. Init preflights the selected dialect JSON and every instruction target and refuses operator-owned data before writing anything. Regression tests cover canonical realm resolution, manifest exclusion, hostile binary refusal without probing, and preservation of dialect files. cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast and BROKKR_HANDS_BOX=1 cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast pass; bundles/self compiles; fmt and clippy -D warnings pass; exact coverage is 19402/19402 lines and 3078/3078 branches. Committed as eb7f2c7; not pushed.

cargo test --workspace: 60 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed the whole delivery — 9c8a95c and the review-return reforge eb7f2c7 — against 544f1d8, with decision 0042 ruling 8 as the commission (init.rs, doctor.rs, their tests, bundle.rs, dialect.rs, quickstart.md, repository-layout.md).

The three medium findings returned to the implementer are FIXED, each re-checked by running the product, not by reading the patch. (1) The scaffolded realm is the repository again: `relative_realm_path` writes `"path": ".."` for `brokkr init my-bundle` and `"."` for `brokkr init .`; I ran init in a scratch OpenSpec repo and then `brokkr doctor` from inside the scaffold exactly as init's success line instructs — it prints `warn dialect starter: openspec … the design route will refuse to run` and `ok dialect starter requires openspec/config.yaml: present at …`, exit 0, where before it printed MISSING and exit 1. realms.json and dialects/ are excluded from the compiled manifest's `files` map (asserted by init_stacks.rs and consistent with realms.rs's own stated rule that adopting a map moves no bundle digest), and the realm data is still pinned with content and sha256 in the RUN manifest by `World::pin`. (2) The unboxed-execution hole is closed at the right layer: `Dialect::check` now refuses a `tool.binary` containing `/`, `\` or `:`, judged by spelling like the instruction paths beside it, and doctor's test proves the probe is never reached for `/bin/echo`. The measured version is passed through `render::Safe`, so a hostile tool cannot inject control characters or forge a second report line. (3) init no longer overwrites operator dialect data: `refuse_dialect_overwrite` checks the dialect JSON and every instruction target, and it runs with the other refusals BEFORE the first byte is written (verified in source order and by the test asserting bundle.json is absent after the refusal).

Constraints re-checked green, by me: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` 0 failures, and 0 failures again with the in-box marker set via `--config 'env.BROKKR_HANDS_BOX="1"'` (the sandbox refuses an env-prefixed cargo invocation, so this was the way in). Exact coverage reproduced from a fresh `cargo +nightly llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --locked --branch --lcov` and the gate's own LCOV accounting: 19402 DA records with 0 uncovered, 3078 BRDA records with 0 untaken, llvm-cov summary functions 1876/1876 — literal 100%. (scripts/coverage-exact.sh itself will not run from a seat; I reproduced its evaluation.) contracts/, fixtures/, policy/phase-machine.json and docs/decisions/README.md are untouched; no harness list and no private-neighbour name enters the prose; tracked tree clean, branch ahead of origin/main by 2 with no remote branch — nothing pushed. My scratch is removed.

Eight findings remain; the highest is LOW, so this is a residual, not a security-hold. Findings 4 and 5 are the two lows carried over from the previous review that the return did not answer.

1. LOW (correctness) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/init.rs:1023 vs crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs:396. init still writes a dialect declaration doctor then hard-fails. init detects spec-kit from `.specify/` being a DIRECTORY; the speckit dialect's `requires` names `.specify/templates/spec-template.md` and `.specify/scripts/bash/check-prerequisites.sh`. Reproduced: `mkdir .specify && brokkr init .` exits 0 having written `"dialect": "speckit"`, and `brokkr doctor` in that same directory then prints two MISSING lines and exits 1 — init's own output fails init's own preflight. A missing required file calls `report.missing`, which clears `healthy`; a missing TOOL warns. Both block exactly the same thing, an artifact phase, and ruling 8 frames the tool case as explicitly not a fail of the whole doctor. Either detect on the files the dialect requires, or warn on a missing required file.

2. LOW (docs) — the guides that show what init writes are now false, and quickstart.md is a guide this slice touches. docs/guides/quickstart.md:155-176 ("What it wrote") lists the scaffold's files exhaustively and omits `./realms.json` and the `./dialects/` tree; quickstart.md:148-153 lists init's refusals and omits the two this slice added (an existing realms.json, existing dialect data). All six pages under docs/guides/starters/ carry the same stale file list and record digests that no longer reproduce — the agents/README.md every scaffold writes gained a `## Specification dialect` section, so every starter digest moved: I ran the tracked rust fixture and got 195ee36f…, where docs/guides/starters/rust.md:36 records d4b6f758d201…. That page states "if these commands ever stop being what `init` writes, a test goes red before this page goes stale"; no test enumerates the scaffold's file set or its digest, so nothing went red. The doctor lines the commission asked for ARE present and correct in both guides — this is the rest of those pages going stale around them.

3. LOW (test integrity) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs:312-319. `#[cfg(test)] fn report_realm_house` is a test-only copy of the production dispatch, kept so the five existing house tests need no edit. Those five (doctor/tests.rs:240, 272, 287, 300, 322) — including `assert_eq!(report.render(), "ok       house rules: no realms map; none declared")` — now assert against a function the binary never calls, and the shipping `Ok(None)` arm at doctor.rs:304-307, which emits TWO lines (house rules and dialect), is asserted by no unit test. Delete the shim and point the five tests at `report_realm`.

4. LOW (SECURITY) — crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs:2751-2758. The new manifest exclusion is silent and by name, and it punches a hole in a fail-closed refusal. The walk `continue`s on any bundle-root entry named `realms.json` or `dialects` before `path.is_dir()`, so nothing under `dialects/` is visited — including the `secrets.env` refusal three lines below, which exists to keep a secrets store out of a bundle. Verified live: a scaffold holding `<bundle>/dialects/secrets.env` compiles clean and prints a digest, where the same file one level up is a hard compile refusal. The harm that refusal names (a secret's sha256 embedded in the manifest, an offline-guessing oracle) does NOT occur, because a skipped file is not hashed — which is why this is low and not medium. What remains is a defensive check with a new blind spot, and a bundle directory that now holds files the digest it prints does not cover, with no line saying so. Refusing or naming the skip would cost one branch.

5. LOW (SECURITY) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs:365. The dialect tool probe has no deadline. `probe(&dialect.tool.binary)` is `Command::new(binary).arg("--version").output()`, which blocks until the child exits; the binary is named by realm data. A realm whose dialect names a PATH binary that never returns on `--version` hangs `brokkr doctor` indefinitely — the one command an operator runs to find out whether a run is safe to start. The same shape already applies to adapter probes, so this is a pre-existing pattern this slice extends to a new data source rather than a new class.

6. INFO (SECURITY, unverified rider on the fixed finding) — the bare-filename rule closes absolute and relative spellings, and on Unix `Command::new` resolves a bare name from PATH only, which is the intended behaviour. On Windows the OS process-search order for a bare application name can include the current directory, in which case a checkout that both declares the dialect and ships an executable of that name could still select it. I did not confirm what current Rust std does here and am not claiming it does; the platform is supported (the code reasons about verbatim prefixes and drive letters), so it is worth one check, and resolving the probe to an explicit PATH hit would settle it either way.

7. INFO (test coverage) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/init.rs:87-127. `OPENSPEC_INSTRUCTIONS` and `SPECKIT_INSTRUCTIONS` are hand-maintained arrays of `include_str!` pairs. Today they match `dialects/openspec/` (6 files) and `dialects/speckit/` (7) exactly, and I confirmed the JSONs' `instructions`, `return_instructions` and `taxonomy` paths are covered. If a future step names a new instruction file and the array is not updated, every scaffold ships a dialect that fails to load, and `init_scaffolds_each_dialect_detection_outcome` would not catch it: it asserts only `<name>.json` and `specify.md`, and `World::load(...).unwrap()` succeeds even when the dialect failed to load — the failure is stored per realm and surfaces only through `dialect_for_realm`. One line, `assert!(world.dialect_for_realm(&world.map.realms[0]).unwrap().is_some())`, closes it.

8. INFO (portability) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/init.rs:1066 and 1047. `realm_path.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/")` mangles a path as a string. When `relative_realm_path` falls through to `common == 0` it returns a CANONICALIZED absolute path, which on Windows carries the `\\?\` verbatim prefix; rewriting its separators yields `//?/C:/…`, which Windows verbatim paths do not accept. Reachable when the bundle and the repository sit on different drives. (A Unix directory whose name contains a literal backslash is corrupted the same way.) The relative arm — the one every ordinary invocation takes — is fine, and no test compares a product-reported path against a test-built path as a string: init_stacks.rs canonicalizes both sides, which is right.

I changed no files, made no commits and ticked no tasks.
